Everyone is so obsessed with that toy.
Hey, quite some time has passed since you came crashing in here.

No, that's not what I mean.
I don't mind at all, no matter who you are or where you're from.
Even if you have a complicated past.
So please stay here forever, okay?
Hey, well then, I'm heading off.
Yeah, take care.

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for one's job or workplace duties.

examples.text: 新しい仕事は楽しいです。
これから仕事に行きます。
examples.trans: I am heading to work now.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

examples.text: もう、ピコピコうるさいなあ。
examples.trans: Geez, all that beeping is so noisy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: i-adjective; used alone as 'Shut up!'.

examples.text: うるさいな、静かにしろ。

meanings.en: sentence-final particle of emotion or reflection
meanings.note: Colloquial particle expressing sighing, wishing, or emphasis.

examples.text: いいなあ、うらやましい。

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').
Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.text: そんなことしたら世の中がめちゃくちゃになりますよ！
examples.trans: If you aired things like that on television, society would fall apart!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Casual, blunt contraction of あなた used between intimates or in heated speech.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: ねえ、あんたが転がり込んできて結構たつじゃない。
examples.trans: Hey, quite some time has passed since you came crashing in here.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: After なくて (隠さなくて結構です), politely says 'there is no need to'.

examples.text: 明日は来なくて結構です。
examples.trans: You do not need to come tomorrow.

examples.text: ねえ、あんたが転がり込んできて結構たつじゃない。
examples.trans: Hey, quite some time has passed since you came crashing in here.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Softens a refusal or correction at the start of a reply.
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for place.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?
Even if you have a complicated past.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

行ってくる.gloss: I'm heading out; I'll be back

meanings.en: I'm heading out; I'll go and come back
meanings.note: Set phrase said when leaving home or the office.

examples.text: ちょっとコンビニに行ってくる。
examples.trans: I'm going to run to the convenience store.

meanings.note: Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: はい、いってきます。行くぞ！
examples.trans: Yes, off I go. Let's move!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
